metadata.title: How to breakthrough disparities in scientific literacy of different family background: The mediating role of self-directed learning efficacy and the moderating role of family support

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata with a two-stage probabilistic sampling design for 15-year-olds in regular/vocational education. The analysis focuses on an East Asia subset (Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, and South Korea) and models relationships among ESCS (family background), SDL efficacy (ST355), family support (ST300), and scientific literacy (PVSCIE1), with gender and grade as controls. The manuscript does not report whether PISA sampling weights (and any replicate weights) were applied in SPSS PROCESS estimation, so weight usage cannot be confirmed from the text. For analysts working with the PISA international database, the recommended approach is to apply the provided student sampling weights (and replicate weights if variance estimation is required) to respect the complex survey design; however, this paper’s specific weighting implementation is not documented.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable is scientific literacy operationalized as the first plausible value (PVSCIE1) from PISA 2022, so plausible-value handling is specified. However, the manuscript does not describe how missing questionnaire or index responses were handled (e.g., whether cases with missing ESCS/SDL efficacy/family support were excluded or imputed). Given that PISA typically contains some missingness in background and scale items, this omission is a reporting gap that prevents assessing potential bias from complete-case selection.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is drawn from PISA 2022 and restricted to an East Asia subset consisting of Hong Kong (China), Macao (China), Taiwan (China), Singapore, Japan, and South Korea. The study uses 15-year-old students in regular/vocational education consistent with PISA’s sampling frame. Scientific literacy is measured using PISA 2022’s scientific literacy plausible values, specifically the first plausible value PVSCIE1. The manuscript does not report additional exclusions (e.g., minimum item response thresholds) or explicit missing-data rules for ESCS, SDL efficacy (ST355), or family support (ST300).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Scientific literacy (PVSCIE1), East Asia subset (Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, South Korea)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Mediation model (PROCESS Model 4): family background → scientific literacy β = 0.211 (p < 0.001); SDL efficacy → scientific literacy β = 0.144 (p < 0.001). Total effect = 24.229 (SE 0.719), direct effect = 21.782 (SE 0.721), indirect (mediating) effect = 2.448 (SE 0.160), with 95% CIs excluding 0 (Table 3).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 scientific literacy data (PVSCIE1) from an East Asia subset, the study leveraged family background (ESCS), SDL efficacy, and controls for grade and gender to predict scientific literacy, finding that family background had a positive direct effect (β = 0.211) and that SDL efficacy carried a significant indirect (mediating) effect (indirect effect = 2.448, 95% CI excluding 0). This indicates that strengthening students’ self-directed learning efficacy may be a practical pathway for reducing science literacy disparities associated with socioeconomic family background, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 SDL efficacy (ST355), East Asia subset (Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, South Korea)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Moderated mediation test (PROCESS Model 7): family background → SDL efficacy β = 0.164 (p < 0.001) in the mediation stage; interaction family background × family support β = 0.033 (p < 0.001). Simple slopes: low family support (M-1SD) simple slope = 0.103 (t = 9.561, p < 0.001); high family support (M+1SD) simple slope = 0.168 (t = 15.389, p < 0.001).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 data on SDL efficacy (ST355) from an East Asia subset, the study leveraged family background (ESCS), family support, and controls for grade and gender to predict SDL efficacy, finding that family support significantly moderated the family background → SDL efficacy relationship (interaction β = 0.033, p < 0.001) with stronger slopes under high family support. This indicates that family-level emotional support may buffer socioeconomic disadvantages by enabling students to translate family resources into higher self-directed learning efficacy, though the observational cross-sectional evidence cannot establish causality.

data.outcome_summary: This Acta Psychologica study uses PISA 2022 microdata restricted to six East Asian societies (Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, and South Korea; total N = 34,968) to examine how family background relates to scientific literacy and through which mechanism. Scientific literacy is modeled using the first plausible value PVSCIE1, while SDL efficacy (ST355) and family support (ST300) are standardized indices. Using SPSS PROCESS (Model 4 for mediation and Model 7 for moderated mediation), the authors report that family background positively predicts scientific literacy (β = 0.211, p < 0.001) and that SDL efficacy significantly mediates the relationship (indirect effect = 2.448; 95% CI excludes 0). They also find that family support strengthens the family background → SDL efficacy link (interaction β = 0.033, p < 0.001; simple slopes 0.103 vs 0.168). Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal identification) and missing-data handling not reported; additionally, the paper does not document whether PISA sampling weights were applied.
